title: Patrick Mahomes and Bo Nix Return From Major Injuries in Chiefs-Broncos Monday Night Matchup
dek: Patrick Mahomes (torn ACL and LCL on December 14, 2025) and Bo Nix (fractured ankle on January 17, 2026) are both fully cleared to play as the Kansas City Chiefs host the Denver Broncos on Monday Night Football. The matchup pits a Chiefs team that finished 6-11 last season against defending AFC West champion Broncos, who posted a 14-3 record and reached the AFC Championship Game.
author: The GoCheckMySports Desk
key_fact: Mahomes tore his ACL and LCL on December 14, 2025, roughly nine months before this matchup; Nix fractured his ankle in the AFC divisional playoff against Buffalo on January 17, 2026. Both quarterbacks are cleared to play.
bottom_line: How Mahomes' restricted mobility after nine months of ACL recovery and Benson's capacity to protect him against Denver's elite pass rush will shape the Chiefs' opening statement in a season where they are rebuilding their secondary and have slipped to third place in a division a defending AFC West champion now owns.
body:
Patrick Mahomes tore his ACL and LCL on December 14, 2025, in a game against Denver. Bo Nix fractured his ankle on January 17, 2026, against Buffalo in the AFC divisional playoff. Both are fully cleared to play Monday night when the Kansas City Chiefs host the Denver Broncos on Monday Night Football at 8:15 p.m. ET, with the game broadcast on ESPN.
The matchup carries weight in the AFC West's power dynamic. The Broncos claimed the No. 1 seed in the AFC last season after a 14-3 record and a trip to the AFC Championship Game, where they lost to the New England Patriots. The Chiefs finished 6-11, missed the playoffs for the first time since 2014, and slipped to third place in the division after winning it in each of the prior nine seasons.
Mahomes' numbers last season reflected struggle before his injury. He completed 62.7 percent of his passes, the lowest of his career, and averaged 7.1 yards per attempt. He threw 22 touchdown passes, also a career low. He did run for 422 yards and five scores. Mahomes said he will not run as much in his return from the ACL tear, a significant constraint given that mobility anchored his offense.
The Chiefs signed running back Kenneth Walker III to a three-year, $43 million contract to address an offensive line that, per CBS Sports, ranks among the least explosive in the NFL over the past two years. Walker surged in the Seattle Seahawks' playoff run last season, taking 65 carries for 313 yards and four touchdowns. He is expected to serve as the full lead back in Kansas City.
Nix arrived as the Broncos' franchise quarterback in his rookie season and has posted consecutive years above 3,700 passing yards and 25 touchdowns. He was 10-7 in Year 1 and 14-3 last season. He had 80-plus rushing attempts in each of his first two seasons and is reportedly at full strength after the ankle injury.
Denver addressed its passing attack by trading three picks (first-round, third-round, and fourth-round) to Miami for Jaylen Waddle and a fourth-rounder. Waddle, who played second fiddle to Tyreek Hill in Miami for most of the past four seasons, is expected to operate as the primary option in Sean Payton's passing attack. Courtland Sutton, the Broncos' established receiver, drew 18 combined targets in the two matchups against Kansas City last season.
The Chiefs will start undrafted rookie Khalil Benson on Mahomes' blind side. The team's left tackle is unavailable for the matchup. Denver's pass rush ranks among the most fearsome in the NFL.
The Chiefs addressed their secondary with three 2026 draft picks: cornerback Mansoor Delane of LSU (first round), defensive tackle Peter Woods of Clemson (second round), and edge rusher R Mason Thomas of Oklahoma (third round). The unit has lost cornerback Trent McDuffie and safety Jaylen Watson to recent departures.
Traveler Travis Kelce, the Chiefs' tight end, averaged around 4.5 receptions per game last season. He recorded a combined 14 catches for 127 yards and a touchdown against Denver in last year's two matchups. Kansas City has not seen Kelce catch fewer than four passes against the Broncos since 2021, per CBS Sports.
Denver has won four of the past five games against Kansas City. The Chiefs won the prior 16 consecutive head-to-head matchups before the recent Broncos run.
